newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: FORECAST-OECD sees Slovak inflation stuck at 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-OECD sees Slovak inflation stuck at 6 pct.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) on Monday forecast Slovakia's annual inflation rate would remain around six percent this year and next year.
"Inflation is projected to stay at around six percent in 1996," the OECD said in its first report devoted to Slovakia.
In its forecast table, the report said inflation would remain at six percent next year too.

The OECD, the Paris-based club of the world's leading industrial economies, said efforts to reduce inflation "may be undermined by demand pressures and necessary relative price adjustments, including those of energy and housing."
The report said substantial further falls in inflation may be difficult to achieve because of the growing strength of Slovakia's economic recovery.
Slovakia's month-on-month inflation was 0.5 percent in August, putting prices 5.6 percent higher than in August last year.
The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has set a 6.0-7.2 percent target range for 1996 inflation, and recently said this appeared achievable. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava, 42-7-210-3687
